chunks: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام was asked about a man who performed six circuits between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah while thinking that they were seven, then remembered after he had exited iḥrām restrictions and had relations with women that he had only performed six. He said:
"He must sacrifice a cow and perform one more circuit."

key_terms.أَحَلَّ: became lawful after a state of restriction
key_terms.أَشْوَاطٍ: circuits or laps of the ritual movement
key_terms.الصَّفَا: al-Ṣafā, one of the two points of saʿy
key_terms.الْمَرْوَةِ: al-Marwah, the other point of saʿy
key_terms.بَقَرَةٌ: a cow to be sacrificed as expiation

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone performs only six circuits of saʿy and realizes it after becoming lawful and having relations with his wife?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding forgetfulness in the saʿy between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah. If a person completed only six circuits, later became lawful, and had marital relations before realizing the deficiency, he must sacrifice a cow and complete the missing circuit.
